    "body": "Curriculum Sequencing Category: Domain-Specific | Level: intermediate | Stability: experimental | Version: v1 Description A curriculum is a directed graph wearing a reading list's clothes. Sequencing it means extracting prerequisite edges from stated dependencies, verifying the graph is acyclic, ordering units topologically, and placing mastery gates between a unit and everything that depends on it. Placement tests adjust the entry point by skipping proven material — not by deleting it, since a skipped unit must remain visible in the path's record. When to Use Use when a set of lessons, modules, or skills must be ordered for a learner — course assembly, onboarding plans, or personalized study paths. Do not use for a flat list with no real dependencies; sorting adds ceremony without value when the graph has no edges. Inputs | Input | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | | | Yes | All learning units in scope | | | | Yes | Stated edges: unit before unit | | | | Yes | Placement results per learner | Procedure 1. Extract prerequisite edges exactly as stated; an assumed-but-unstated dependency is an edge nobody can audit. 2. Detect cycles first; a cyclic curriculum has no valid order, only a hidden wrong edge to fix. 3. Produce a topological order of the units; ties break deterministically (by unit id) for reproducible plans. 4. Apply placement: units already mastered are marked skipped-in-place, never removed from the record. 5. Insert m astery gates before dependents: a unit's dependents unlock only when its gate is passed. 6. Emit the path with per-unit status (assigned, skipped, gated) and the edge set it was derived from. Outputs | Output | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | | | The dependency-respecting order | | | | The offending units, if the graph is cyclic | | | | Units whose mastery gates downstream dependents | Runnable Example Failure Modes | Failure Mode | Cause | Mitigation | |---|---|---| | Circular prerequisites | Units that depend on each other transitively | Detect cycles before ordering; fix the graph | | Hidden prerequisites | Assumed knowledge not stated as edges | Make every dependency an explicit, auditable edge | | Ungated advancement | Dependents reached before mastery | Insert mastery gates before dependents | | Placement amnesia | Skipped units vanish from records | Mark skipped-in-place; keep the full path visible | | Orphan units | Units no path can reach | Surface unreachable units for graph repair | Security and Authority Boundary Sequencing ord ers material; it certifies nothing about mastery.     "body": "Customer Churn Analysis Category: Domain-Specific | Level: intermediate | Stability: experimental | Version: v1 Description Churn analysis is only useful when it changes what a team does next. The skill covers defining churn operationally, joining behavioral signals with observed outcomes, building interpretable risk features, and validating that signals precede churn rather than accompany it. The deliverable is a ranked intervention list with per-signal evidence, plus the honest note that association is not a retention mechanism. When to Use Use when a subscription or recurring-revenue business must understand and predict which customers are likely to leave and why. Do not treat every correlated metric as a churn cause. Intervening on a signal that merely accompanies churn wastes retention budget and can irritate customers. Inputs | Input | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | | | Yes | Per-account events, usage, and status changes over time | | | | Yes | Observed churn or retention outcomes per account | | | | Yes | Feature window and prediction horizon definitions | Procedure 1. Define churn operationally: cancellation event, lapse, or inactivity threshold, with the observation window. 2. Join behavioral signals with outcomes using strict temporal windows: features precede the outcome. 3. Build interpretable features: usage trend, support contacts, billing failures, and engagement drop. 4. Score accounts for churn risk with the model kept simple enough to explain per account. 5. Validate that top signals are leading, not coincident, using lagged analysis. 6. Emit a ranked intervention list with per-account evidence and stated confidence. Outputs | Output | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | | | Per-account churn risk with top contributing signals | | | | Per-signal strength and lead time before churn | | | | Accounts ranked with suggested actions and caveats | Runnable Example Failure Modes | Failure Mode | Cause | Mitigation | |---|---|---| | Coincident signals treated as causes | Interventions fired on symptoms | Lag analysis before ranking any signal | | Churn defined inconsistently | Lapse and inactivity conflated | One operational definition stated up front | | Feature leakage | Post-churn behavior used as a feature | Enforce the feature window strictly | | Retention theater | Discounts to accounts that would stay anyway | Target by risk band, not blanket offers | | Survivor bias in validation | Only completed windows evaluated | Include censored accounts in evaluation | Security and Authority Boundary Churn models segment real customers by behavior.     "description": "Map clinical descriptions to standard diagnosis codes using literal text support, a supplied code index, and explicit unresolved-case flagging so every code emitted is traceable, never invented.",
    "body": "Diagnosis Coding Category: Domain-Specific | Level: advanced | Stability: experimental | Version: v1 Description Diagnosis coding is a lookup task with a discipline problem: the temptation to code what a clinician probably meant. This skill pins the process to text — a code may be emitted only when the clinical text literally supports it, lookups run against a supplied code index of the declared version, and cases that cannot be resolved are flagged for a human coder. Output pairs every code with its evidence span, so nothing in the coded record is unattributable. When to Use Use when clinical notes or symptom descriptions must be converted to a standard code system (ICD or a supplied local variant) for administrative structuring. Do not use to diagnose patients, and do not emit codes for what the text implies but does not say; implication is a clinical judgment, not a coding fact. Inputs | Input | Type | Required | Description | |---|---|---|---| | | | Yes | The note or description to code | | | | Yes | The declared code system and version | | | | Yes | Supplied index mapping codes to matching terms | | | | No | Restriction to an allowed code subset | Procedure 1. Declare the code system and version before lookup; codes from mixed versions do not merge into one record. 2. Normalize the clinical text conservatively — case and whitespace, not paraphrase; the evidence span must survive. 3. Match only against the supplied index, restricted to the declared scope if one is given. 4. Emit a code only with a literal evidence span from the source text; the span is part of the output. 5. Flag unresolved cases explicitly for human coding; a near-miss is a flag, not a code with a lower bar. 6. Record code, span, code system version, and confidence; audits reconstruct every decision from these fields. Outputs | Output | Type | Description | |---|---|---| | | | Emitted codes with their evidence spans | | | | Index entries needing human coding | | | | Code system, version, and per-code confidence | Runnable Example Failure Modes | Failure Mode | Cause | Mitigation | |---|---|---| | Plausible-but-unsupported codes | Coding the likely diagnosis, not the stated one | Require a literal evidence span per code | | Category drift | Symptoms coded as diagnoses | Keep symptom codes distinct and scope-restricted | | Mixed code versions | Codes from different releases in one record | Declare one system version per record | | Abbreviation ambiguity | Short forms with multiple expansions | Flag ambiguous abbreviations for human coding | | Silent substitution | Model codes where a human must | Emit flags, never substitutions, for unresolved cases | Security and Authority Boundary Coding support is administrative structuring of clinical text; it is not a diagnosis and not medical advice. Diagnostic decisions stay with licensed clinicians, and coded output must be reviewed under the facility's coding compliance process.     "body": "Receipt Parsing Category: Domain-Specific | Level: intermediate | Stability: experimental | Version: v1 Description A receipt is unstructured text pretending to be a table. Parsing it means segmentation (header, items, totals), normalization (dates, currencies, decimal separators per locale), and — the part that separates data from guesswork — arithmetic verification: line items must sum to the subtotal, and subtotal plus tax must match the stated total. Every extracted field carries its raw span, so any number in the structured record can be traced to where it came from. When to Use Use when receipt text (typed or OCR output) must become structured expense data — bookkeeping automation, reimbursement workflows, spend analysis. Normalize numbers per locale — decimal separator, currency symbol, thousands grouping — before any arithmetic. 3. Parse line items as (quantity, description, amount) triples; wrapped descriptions are joined, not split into items. 4. Cross-check: it em sum against stated subtotal; subtotal plus tax against stated total; record the verdict per check. 5.
